title: Contract Verbs
description: Verbs in -άω, -έω and -όω: the rules of contraction and the lengthened vowel of the other tenses.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html: In the present system (present and imperfect) the final vowel of these stems contracts with the variable vowel. ε + ε makes ει, ε + ο makes ου, ε before a long vowel or diphthong disappears (φιλέω, φιλῶ; φιλέομεν, φιλοῦμεν). α + an ο-sound makes ω, α + an ε-sound makes long α (τιμάομεν, τιμῶμεν; τιμάετε, τιμᾶτε). ο + a long vowel makes ω, ο + a short vowel or ου makes ου, and any combination with ι makes οι (δηλόομεν, δηλοῦμεν; δηλόει, δηλοῖ). The contracted syllable is accented with a circumflex if the first of the two vowels had the acute. Lexicons list the uncontracted first person (τιμάω), so that the conjugation is known.

blocks.caption: φιλέω, τιμάω, δηλόω: present active indicative
rows: Infinitives: φιλεῖν, τιμᾶν, δηλοῦν. Participles: φιλῶν, φιλοῦσα, φιλοῦν; τιμῶν, τιμῶσα, τιμῶν; δηλῶν, δηλοῦσα, δηλοῦν. Imperfect: ἐφίλουν, ἐτίμων, ἐδήλουν.

blocks.caption: The other tenses
blocks.html: Outside the present system there is no contraction: the stem vowel is lengthened before the tense suffix (ε and α to η, ο to ω): φιλήσω, ἐφίλησα, ἐφιλήθην; τιμήσω; δηλώσω, ἐδηλώθην. καλέω is an exception: καλέσω, ἐκάλεσα, and the aorist passive ἐκλήθην.

blocks.caption: Common confusion
blocks.html: ἀγαπῶμεν is both "we love" and "let us love" (the indicative and subjunctive of -άω verbs fall together); ἀγαπῶσι(ν) is both "they love" and "to those who love". The context decides.
